<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par134 />{{GHGmargin-letter|134|d}}
Rem. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=24|verse=22}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} follows the construct state {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁפַּט}}, but here as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=15|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁפָּט}} should be read. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} is in apposition to a substantive with a suffix (= ''one of you brethren''; but verse 33 ''the one of you brethren''). In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶחָד}} precedes the substantive in the Aramaic manner (= ''one each'').—For {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָֽה־שָׁנָה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, &c.) we find regularly in the Priestly Code (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=1|hidebook=1}}) {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת שָׁנָה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=3}}, &c.) ''an hundred years''. On the connexion of abstract numerals with suffixes, as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵיהֶם|translate=their duality}}, i.e. ''they two'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}, &c. (also with a strengthening separate pronoun, as {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵ֫ינוּ אֲנַ֫חְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=42}}), cf. {{GHGpar|97|i}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|e}}
'''2.''' The numerals from 2 to 10 take the object numbered in the plural,<ref>On examples such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27}} ({{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֫יִם|translate=two souls}}), cf. {{GHGpar|132|g}} (collectives joined with the plural of the adjective).</ref> with very few exceptions, such as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=22}} (where {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵי הָעֹ֫מֶר}} = ''the double of an omer''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=45|verse=1}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=17}} and 25:17 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}} The numerals from 11 to 19 generally take the plural, but with certain substantives frequently used with numerals the singular is more common (see further, under ''f''). The tens (from 20 to 90), when they precede, take the singular (in the accusative, cf. {{GHGpar|131|p}}) of certain nouns frequently used with numerals ({{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף|translate=a thousand}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל}}—but only in Ezekiel and the Priestly Code), otherwise the plural, as {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּנוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=עָרִים}} (but cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=33}}), &c.; on the other hand, the plural is necessary when they follow the object numbered in apposition (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַמּוֹת עֶשְׂרִים|translate=twenty cubits}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=3|verse=3}} f.; with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=24}}, only in late Books). After {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה}} and {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}} the substantive numbered may be used either in the singular or plural, see further under ''g''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|f}}
Rem. 1. After the numerals from 11 to 19 the singular is used, as a rule, with {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם|translate=day}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה|translate=year}}, {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ|translate=man}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=soul}} (person), {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁ֫בֶט|translate=tribe}}, {{GHGheb|text=מַצֵּבָה|translate=pillar}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=24|verse=4}}), sometimes with {{GHGheb|text=אַמָּה|translate=cubit}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֹ֫דֶשׁ|translate=month}}, {{GHGheb|text=עִיר|translate=city}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל|translate=shekel}} (compare our ''four-year-old, ten pound''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם}} (cf., however, such exceptions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=4|verse=2}}, &c.).—Substantives other than these are used in the plural with the numerals from 11 to 19, and the numeral may even follow the substantive, especially in later passages, as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=7|verse=87}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=25|verse=5|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|134|g}}
2. After {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה}} ({{GHGheb|text=מְאַת}} [so almost exclusively in the Priestly Code, e.g. always {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת אֶ֫לֶף}}], {{GHGheb|text=מֵאוֹת}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָאתַ֫יִם}}) and {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲלָפִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפֵי}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַלְפַּ֫יִם}}) the substantives {{GHGheb|text=אִישׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫לֶף}}, {{GHGheb|text=אַמָּה}} (except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=27}}), {{GHGheb|text=יוֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַגְלִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֶ֫מֶד}} are regularly used in the singular, generally also {{GHGheb|text=שָׁנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֹּר}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫קֶל}} (with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=26}}, &c.); cf., moreover, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=33|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=60|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַלְפֵי רְבָבָה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=1|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=9|verse=15}}.—Examples of the ''plural'' after {{GHGheb|text=מֵאָה}} are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=4}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מְאַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=27}}; after {{GHGheb|text=מֵאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=17}},<section end=par134 /><noinclude>
